identity_marker: the silver and black AccuBANKER AB-5000 bill counter with a top hopper and front LCD screen
continuity_anchors: on a flat wooden desk under bright, even overhead office lighting
video_goal: Demonstrate how to efficiently and accurately count a retail cash drawer using the AccuBANKER AB-5000 bill counter.
single_prompt: A close-up shows a hand flipping the rear power switch of the silver and black AccuBANKER AB-5000 bill counter with a top hopper and front LCD screen, illuminating the screen with a blue backlight on a flat wooden desk under bright, even overhead office lighting. From an over-the-shoulder view, two hands lift a black plastic cash drawer filled with sorted bills and coins, placing it to the left of the machine. A close-up reveals an index finger pressing the 'MODE' button until 'MIX' appears on the display. From a high-angle view, a hand reaches into the far-right compartment of the cash drawer, lifts the metal spring clip, and pulls out a thick stack of $1 bills. At eye-level, two hands tap the edges of the $1 bill stack against the desk to align them perfectly. A close-up shows the hand placing the aligned stack into the top hopper, sliding them back to trigger the feed sensor. A macro shot captures the rubber rollers spinning rapidly, pulling the bills down into the bottom stacker. A close-up focuses on the LCD screen numbers ticking up rapidly to display a final piece count of '45' and a total value of '$45'. At eye-level, a hand grasps the neatly stacked $1 bills from the bottom stacker and pulls them out. From an over-the-shoulder view, a hand holding a pen writes '45.00' on the '$1' line of a paper tally sheet. A high-angle view shows the hand reaching back into the cash drawer, lifting the second metal clip, and pulling out a stack of $5 bills. Finally, a close-up shows the hand dropping the squared $5 bills into the top hopper, and the rollers immediately begin spinning to count the new stack.
